Solution 1 has the correct answer, 3. Solutions 2 and 3 are wrong.

**Why the set is so restricted.** Membership in $\mathcal P$ is closed under induced subgraphs, so any $H$ that fails $\mathcal P$ kills everything above it. Some hereditary classes of unbounded clique-width rule out each candidate below.

- **$K_3$ fails.** Its subdivisions are all cycles $C_k$, $k\ge 3$, so the class is chordal graphs. Chordal graphs include split graphs, which have unbounded clique-width. Solution 2's inclusion of $C_3$ is therefore wrong.
- **$3K_1$ and $K_{1,3}$ fail.** Complements of grids are $3K_1$-free and have unbounded clique-width. Claw-free graphs (such as line graphs of grids) have no induced subdivided claw, so the claw fails too.
- **$C_4$ fails.** Its subdivisions are cycles of length $\ge 4$, so the class is chordal graphs again.
- **$2K_2$ fails.** Split graphs are $2K_2$-free and have unbounded clique-width.
- **$C_5$ fails.** Its subdivisions are the induced cycles of length $\ge 5$. Chordal bipartite graphs have no odd holes, so they avoid induced $C_5$ subdivisions. They have unbounded clique-width (Golumbic–Rotics), so $C_5$ fails.

**What survives.** Any $H$ satisfying $\mathcal P$ must be triangle-free, $C_4$-free, $2K_2$-free and have independence number at most 2. Triangle-free with $\alpha\le 2$ forces $|V(H)|\le 5$ (since $R(3,3)=6$). On 5 vertices the only such graph is $C_5$, which fails. On 4 vertices the only survivor is $P_4$. Every smaller survivor is an induced subgraph of $P_4$.

**$P_4$ does satisfy $\mathcal P$.** Its induced subdivisions are the paths $P_k$ with $k\ge 4$, so the class is exactly $P_4$-free graphs (cographs), which have clique-width at most 2.

So $\mathcal M=\{P_4\}$, the set of edge counts is $\{3\}$, and the sum is 3.

Solution 3's pan-free step is also wrong: $C_5$ with a pendant vertex is an induced subdivision of the paw but contains no induced pan.

CHOICE: 1
